title: Purchase tags fire on a thank-you page view or without an order ID
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: Every Purchase tag (GA4, Meta, Snap, TikTok, Google Ads) fires on the dataLayer purchase event, not on a thank-you page view, and sends the order's transaction_id (or the platform's order id / event_id).
fails: A Purchase or conversion tag fires on a page-view trigger matching the thank-you URL, so a refresh or a back-button visit sends the order again; or no transaction_id is sent, so GA4 can't drop the repeat.
validate: GTM read: list every purchase/conversion tag for each platform, its firing trigger (custom event vs page view + URL filter) and whether transaction_id (or the platform's order id) is mapped to an order variable. Fail on any URL-based purchase trigger or missing order id. Checkout is not observed in the browser, so the verdict comes from the container only.
action: Ask the developer to fire every Purchase tag on the dataLayer purchase event and send the order id with it.
done_when: No purchase or conversion tag in the live container uses a page-view or URL trigger, and each one sends the order id.
why_it_matters: A repeat Purchase makes reported ROAS read higher than real, so losing campaigns can look like winners and get scaled; fixing it may lower reported ROAS, which is the truth showing.
selected_because: The setup that causes double purchases, read from the container; GA4's order data shows the effect as a separate finding.

title: Shopify checkout purchases actually reach the platforms
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: The store is not on Shopify, or begin_checkout and Purchase for each platform come from a Shopify Customer Events pixel or the platform's native Shopify app.
fails: A Shopify store relies on GTM tags for checkout and Purchase, but GTM does not run inside Shopify checkout, so those events never fire.
validate: Crawl/browser: detect Shopify. GTM read: find begin_checkout and Purchase tags and check whether they rely on triggers that can only fire inside checkout. Browser: look for the Shopify web pixel manager loading custom or app pixels on storefront pages. Checkout itself is not observed; say so.
action: Ask the developer to send checkout and Purchase from a Shopify Customer Events custom pixel or the platform's own Shopify app, not from GTM.
done_when: No platform depends on a GTM-only Purchase tag on Shopify, and a custom or app pixel for each paid platform is visible on the storefront.
why_it_matters: Sales that never fire make reported ROAS read lower than real, so winning campaigns can get cut and the algorithm learns from fewer purchases.
selected_because: A whole-store under-count on the most common platform; readable from container plus platform detection.

title: Purchase tags mapped to value, currency and items
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: Every platform's Purchase tag (GA4, Meta, Snap, TikTok, Google Ads) reads value as a number, the store's currency (SAR, AED, EGP and so on) and items from dataLayer variables whose paths match the store's purchase push.
fails: On a Purchase tag, value or currency is missing, hard-typed, or read from a mistyped dataLayer path that returns undefined, or items/contents are not mapped.
validate: GTM read: for each platform's Purchase tag, the value, currency and items/contents parameters and the variables behind them (paths such as ecommerce.value, ecommerce.currency, ecommerce.items, and any constant or Custom JavaScript used instead). Purchase is not observed in the browser, so the container is the only place its payload can be checked.
action: Ask the developer to map value, currency and items from one set of dataLayer variables into every platform's Purchase tag.
done_when: Every Purchase tag reads value, currency and items from dataLayer variables with the store's real paths.
why_it_matters: Without value and currency on Purchase the platforms can't see revenue, so reported ROAS reads low or blank and value-based bidding has nothing to learn from.
selected_because: Revenue the platforms never see; the Purchase payload is only checkable in the container because the visit stops at the cart.

title: Consent default set first in the container, per region
group_en: Consent that doesn't hide your sales
group_ar: الـ consent من غير ما يخبّي مبيعاتك
pass: The consent template fires on Consent Initialization - All Pages before any other tag, its defaults are set per region (denied where the law requires it, granted where it doesn't, for example GCC and Egypt), and each ad tag's consent settings match the banner categories.
fails: The consent default fires late on a page-view trigger, denies every tag in every region, or ad tags carry no or wrong consent settings, so Meta, Snap, TikTok and Google tags stay silent for visitors who never touch the banner or ignore the choice.
validate: GTM read: the consent/CMP tag's trigger and firing order, its default parameters and region lists, and the consent settings on each Meta, Snap, TikTok, GA4 and Google Ads tag.
action: Ask the developer to move the consent default to Consent Initialization, set it per region so GCC and Egypt visits record normally, and give every ad tag consent settings that match the banner.
done_when: The consent default fires on Consent Initialization with region rules, and every ad tag has consent settings that match the banner categories.
why_it_matters: Blocked tags hide real sales from every platform, so reported ROAS reads lower than real and the algorithm learns from a fraction of buyers.
selected_because: Tested in audits (2 of 4 failed the default); the container setup behind consent, while the page-code list reads the consent state on live hits.

title: Meta events carry an event_id for CAPI dedupe
group_en: Meta: Pixel, CAPI and fbclid
group_ar: Meta: الـ Pixel والـ CAPI والـ fbclid
pass: Every Meta Purchase and AddToCart tag sends an event_id from one shared variable that the Conversions API feed can reuse, unique per event.
fails: The Pixel sends no event_id, or a fixed or reused value, so Pixel and CAPI copies of one sale can't be matched.
validate: GTM read: eventID parameter on Meta Purchase and AddToCart tags and the variable behind it (unique per event, not a constant). Browser: the eid parameter on the live AddToCart hit after our click. Whether CAPI uses the same id is not visible from here; say so.
action: Ask the developer to send a unique event_id on Meta Pixel events and pass the same id to the Conversions API.
done_when: Meta Purchase and AddToCart tags read eventID from a per-event variable, and the live AddToCart hit shows an eid.
why_it_matters: With Pixel plus CAPI and no shared event_id, Meta can count a sale twice, so reported ROAS reads higher than real.
selected_because: event_id dedupe is named in the spec; the browser side is fully checkable.

title: Meta tags set up for every funnel step
group_en: Meta: Pixel, CAPI and fbclid
group_ar: Meta: الـ Pixel والـ CAPI والـ fbclid
pass: The container (or the Meta app) has ViewContent, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout and Purchase tags, each on the matching event, and the Pixel base code fires before them.
fails: Meta paid traffic shows in GA4 but the container only sends PageView, Purchase or InitiateCheckout has no tag, or event tags fire before the base code loads and get dropped.
validate: GA4 report: sessionSource/medium for facebook, instagram, meta paid traffic. GTM read: Meta tags for ViewContent, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout and Purchase, their triggers, and tag sequencing or priority so the base code fires first. Browser cross-check: ViewContent on the product page and AddToCart after our click on facebook.com/tr.
action: Ask the developer to add the missing Meta events and fire the Pixel base code before them.
done_when: Tags for all four Meta events exist on the matching dataLayer events, sequenced after the base code, and ViewContent and AddToCart are seen live.
why_it_matters: Missing funnel events leave Meta optimising on thin signal, so delivery finds fewer buyers and CAC likely runs higher than it needs to.
selected_because: Meta leads tracked spend; base-before-events was tested (2 of 3 stores failed). Per-event setup, distinct from whether a pixel loads at all.

title: Container sends data to IDs the store doesn't own
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: Every GA4, Meta, Snap, TikTok and Google Ads tag in the live container uses the store's own ID, ideally from one constant variable per platform, and no paused, triggerless or ex-agency tag is left.
fails: Tags hold hard-coded or old IDs (a past agency's pixel, a second GA4 property), or dead tags from past vendors still fire, so part of the signal goes to an account you don't optimise.
validate: GTM read: list every tag's platform and ID (direct or through variables), paused tags, tags with no trigger, and IDs that differ from the main one per platform; output the list for the buyer to match against the ad accounts they run.
action: Confirm which IDs belong to your ad accounts, then ask the developer to remove the rest and move each ID into one constant variable.
done_when: Each platform has one ID in the live container and it is one you confirmed.
why_it_matters: Events sent to an old or foreign pixel never reach the account you bid in, so that account learns from fewer sales and reported ROAS reads lower than real.
selected_because: Backfill: the container-only view of stray and ex-vendor IDs; the live double-hit check stays in the page-code list.

title: Server route for Meta CAPI, Snap CAPI and TikTok Events API
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: A server-side route for ad events is visible: a server GTM container (server_container_url or transport_url), first-party collection hits, or a detected platform app that sends server events, for each paid platform.
fails: Every paid platform is browser-pixel only, so purchases blocked by ad blockers, Safari or iOS limits never reach Meta, Snap or TikTok.
validate: GTM read: server_container_url / transport_url on the Google tag, server-bound tags or templates for Meta CAPI, Snap CAPI or TikTok Events API. Browser: hits to a first-party collection subdomain. Crawl: platform app scripts that offer server events. If an app is present but its server events can't be seen, mark 'not visible from outside', not failed.
action: Ask the developer to add a server route (server GTM or each platform's server integration) for Purchase on Meta, Snap and TikTok, with the same event_id as the Pixel.
done_when: A server route is visible in the container or network for each paid platform.
why_it_matters: Browser-only tracking misses blocked sales, so reported ROAS reads lower than real and the algorithm learns from fewer buyers.
selected_because: Tested (2 of 5 stores had no server route); kept to what the container and network show, no Events Manager data.

title: Conversion tags that fire on every page
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: Purchase, Add to Cart and lead conversion tags fire only on their own event, with trigger conditions (or trigger groups) that require every needed condition, never on All Pages.
fails: A conversion tag sits on All Pages, on a broad page-view trigger with no condition, or on a trigger group missing a condition, so it fires on visits that are not conversions.
validate: GTM read: the triggers on each conversion tag across platforms; flag All Pages, page-view triggers with no URL or event condition, and trigger groups that miss a required condition.
action: Ask the developer to put each conversion tag on its own event trigger and remove All Pages from it.
done_when: No conversion tag in the live container fires on All Pages or an unconditioned trigger.
why_it_matters: A conversion tag on every page counts visits as sales or adds, so reported conversions and ROAS read higher than real and the algorithm chases the wrong people.
selected_because: Backfill: an over-count cause read directly from trigger conditions.

title: Add to Cart tags triggered by a button click, not the add event
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: Every platform's Add to Cart tag fires on the store's add-to-cart dataLayer event (or the theme's AJAX add event), not on a click, CSS-selector or form-submit trigger.
fails: Add to Cart fires on a button-click or selector trigger, so it counts clicks that add nothing (no variant chosen, out of stock), or on a form-submit trigger that misses drawer and quick adds.
validate: GTM read: the trigger type and conditions behind each platform's Add to Cart tag (custom event vs click, element selector or form submit).
action: Ask the developer to trigger Add to Cart from the store's add-to-cart event, not from the button click.
done_when: Every Add to Cart tag uses a custom-event trigger on the store's add event.
why_it_matters: A click-based Add to Cart feeds the algorithm false intent, so ATC-optimised campaigns and retargeting audiences are built on clicks that weren't adds.
selected_because: The trigger setup behind Add to Cart counts; our live click shows whether the event arrives, this shows whether it can fire on clicks that add nothing.

title: Google Ads conversion tag, Conversion Linker and Enhanced Conversions set
group_en: Google: Ads conversions and Consent Mode v2
group_ar: Google: الـ conversions والـ Consent Mode v2
pass: When Google Ads runs, the container has a Google Ads conversion tag (or GA4 import is used), a Conversion Linker on all pages, and Enhanced Conversions with user-provided data set on the conversion tag.
fails: Google Ads traffic shows in GA4 but there is no conversion tag or Conversion Linker, or Enhanced Conversions is not set in the tag.
validate: GA4 report: google / cpc traffic. GTM read: awct and Conversion Linker tags, their triggers, and the conversion tag's user-provided-data setting. The Google Ads account side is not checked; say so.
action: Ask the developer to add the Google Ads conversion tag, a Conversion Linker on all pages and Enhanced Conversions in the tag.
done_when: The container has a conversion tag with user-provided data and a Conversion Linker on all pages.
why_it_matters: Missing conversions or no Conversion Linker leave Smart Bidding with fewer sales, so Google's reported ROAS reads lower than real.
selected_because: Google is the fourth platform in the spec; container setup only, the gclid survival test sits with the live click-ID check.

title: Snap tags set up for the funnel your Snap ads need
group_en: Snapchat: Snap Pixel, CAPI and ScCid
group_ar: Snapchat: الـ Snap Pixel والـ CAPI والـ ScCid
pass: When Snapchat sends traffic, the container (or the Snap app) has VIEW_CONTENT, ADD_CART and PURCHASE tags on the matching events.
fails: Snapchat paid traffic shows in GA4 but only PAGE_VIEW is set up, or PURCHASE has no tag.
validate: GA4 report: sessionSource for snapchat paid traffic. GTM read: Snap tags for VIEW_CONTENT, ADD_CART and PURCHASE and their triggers. Browser cross-check: tr.snapchat.com hits for VIEW_CONTENT on the product page and ADD_CART after our click.
action: Ask the developer to add the missing Snap events: VIEW_CONTENT, ADD_CART and PURCHASE.
done_when: Tags for all three Snap events exist on the matching events, and VIEW_CONTENT and ADD_CART are seen live.
why_it_matters: Without Snap events, Snap campaigns optimise on clicks instead of buyers, so CAC on Snap likely runs higher than it needs to.
selected_because: Snapchat leads reach in KSA; spec says score it after Meta. Per-event setup, distinct from whether the pixel loads.

title: Snap events carry a dedupe id for Snap CAPI
group_en: Snapchat: Snap Pixel, CAPI and ScCid
group_ar: Snapchat: الـ Snap Pixel والـ CAPI والـ ScCid
pass: The Snap PURCHASE (and ADD_CART) tag sends client_dedup_id from a unique per-event variable that the Snap Conversions API feed can reuse.
fails: No dedupe id, or a fixed value, so a Pixel sale and its CAPI copy can't be matched.
validate: GTM read: client_dedup_id (or the template's dedupe field) on Snap PURCHASE and ADD_CART tags and the variable behind it. Browser: the dedupe field on the live ADD_CART hit. Whether Snap CAPI sends the same id is not visible; say so.
action: Ask the developer to send a unique client_dedup_id on Snap events and the same id from Snap CAPI.
done_when: Snap PURCHASE and ADD_CART tags read a per-event dedupe id, and the live ADD_CART hit carries one.
why_it_matters: Pixel plus CAPI without a shared id can count one Snap sale twice, so Snap's reported ROAS reads higher than real.
selected_because: Snap pixel/CAPI dedupe requested for this persona; browser side checkable.

title: TikTok tags set up for the funnel your TikTok ads need
group_en: TikTok: pixel, Events API and ttclid
group_ar: TikTok: الـ Pixel والـ Events API والـ ttclid
pass: When TikTok sends traffic, the container (or the TikTok app) has ViewContent, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout and CompletePayment (or Purchase) tags on the matching events.
fails: TikTok paid traffic shows in GA4 but only PageView is set up, or the purchase event has no tag.
validate: GA4 report: sessionSource for tiktok paid traffic. GTM read: TikTok tags for ViewContent, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout and CompletePayment/Purchase and their triggers. Browser cross-check: analytics.tiktok.com hits for ViewContent on the product page and AddToCart after our click.
action: Ask the developer to add the TikTok events that are missing.
done_when: Tags for all four TikTok events exist on the matching events, and ViewContent and AddToCart are seen live.
why_it_matters: Without TikTok events, TikTok optimises on clicks instead of buyers, so CAC on TikTok likely runs higher than it needs to.
selected_because: TikTok named in the persona spec; per-event setup, distinct from whether the pixel loads.

title: TikTok events carry an event_id for Events API dedupe
group_en: TikTok: pixel, Events API and ttclid
group_ar: TikTok: الـ Pixel والـ Events API والـ ttclid
pass: The TikTok purchase and AddToCart tags send an event_id from a unique per-event variable that the Events API feed can reuse.
fails: No event_id, or a fixed value, so pixel and Events API copies of one sale can't be matched.
validate: GTM read: event_id on TikTok purchase and AddToCart tags and the variable behind it. Browser: event_id on the live AddToCart hit. Whether the Events API sends the same id is not visible; say so.
action: Ask the developer to send a unique event_id on TikTok pixel events and the same id from the Events API.
done_when: TikTok purchase and AddToCart tags read a per-event event_id, and the live AddToCart hit carries one.
why_it_matters: Pixel plus Events API without a shared event_id can count one sale twice, so TikTok's reported ROAS reads higher than real.
selected_because: TikTok Events API dedupe requested for this persona; browser side checkable.

title: Click-ID and analytics cookies last long enough
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: _ga, _fbc, _gcl_aw and the Snap and TikTok first-party cookies are set with a lifetime that covers a normal consideration window, and cookie variables in GTM read the right cookie names.
fails: Cookies are set by script with a short or session-only lifetime, or a GTM cookie variable points at a wrong name, so a buyer who returns days after the ad click is no longer tied to it.
validate: Browser (Chromium): after landing with test click IDs, read each cookie's expiry and whether it was set by script or by an HTTP header. GTM read: first-party cookie variables and their names compared with the cookies seen live. Safari and Firefox behaviour is not checked; say so.
action: Ask the developer to set click-ID and analytics cookies with a long first-party lifetime (server-set where possible) and fix cookie variable names.
done_when: Every checked cookie has a lifetime longer than a session, and each GTM cookie variable matches a cookie seen live.
why_it_matters: Short cookies cut the link between the ad click and a later purchase, so returning buyers show as direct and reported ROAS reads lower than real.
selected_because: High value for purchases made days after the click (I 4); about cookie lifetime, not whether the click ID arrives.

title: WhatsApp clicks tracked as a signal
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: The store has no WhatsApp or phone links, or clicks on them fire a GA4 event and a pixel event (for example Meta Contact) with the page.
fails: The site has wa.me, api.whatsapp.com or tel: links and no tag tracks them, so orders that start in WhatsApp never reach GA4 or the ad platforms.
validate: Browser: WhatsApp and tel: links found on home, product and cart. GTM read: link-click triggers on wa.me / api.whatsapp.com / tel: and the tags they fire.
action: Ask the developer to track WhatsApp and call clicks in GA4 and in each paid platform's pixel.
done_when: A click on the store's WhatsApp link fires a GA4 event and a pixel event.
why_it_matters: WhatsApp orders that never fire an event make your campaigns look like they sell less than they do, so reported ROAS reads lower than real.
selected_because: Spec names WhatsApp orders that never fire as an under-count; links and triggers are both visible.

title: Accepting the banner late still credits the ad
group_en: Consent that doesn't hide your sales
group_ar: الـ consent من غير ما يخبّي مبيعاتك
pass: When a banner shows, a visitor who lands from an ad and accepts a few seconds later still gets a page_view and pixel PageView with the original UTMs and click IDs.
fails: Tags wait for consent, then fire without the landing parameters, so the session is credited to direct and the click ID is lost.
validate: Browser: open a landing URL with test UTMs and fbclid/ttclid/ScCid; wait; accept the banner; check that the first GA4 page_view and each pixel hit after accepting carry the test values. If no banner shows to our visit, mark not applicable.
action: Ask the developer to keep the landing parameters and send them with the first hits after consent.
done_when: After a late accept, the first GA4 and pixel hits carry the test UTMs and click IDs.
why_it_matters: Visitors who accept late get credited to direct, so paid campaigns look weaker than they are and reported ROAS reads low.
selected_because: A consent-timing leak that hides paid credit; testable with one accept in the headless run.

title: Built-in variables your triggers need are switched on
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: Built-in variables used by triggers and tags (Page URL, Page Path, Click URL, Click Element, Event and the form variables) are enabled in the container.
fails: A trigger or tag condition refers to a built-in variable that is switched off, so the trigger never fires as built and the tag stays silent.
validate: GTM read: list_built_in_variables compared with the variables referenced in trigger filters and tag fields; flag any reference to a disabled built-in.
action: Ask the developer to enable the missing built-in variables and test the affected tags in Preview.
done_when: No trigger or tag refers to a disabled built-in variable.
why_it_matters: A trigger that never fires means its events never reach GA4 or the platforms, so the conversions behind it go uncounted and reported ROAS reads lower than real.
selected_because: Backfill: a silent cause of missing events, fully readable in the container.

title: Pixels pasted as Custom HTML and unknown scripts
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: Meta, Snap, TikTok and Google tags use the official GTM templates or the store platform's integration, and every remaining Custom HTML tag has a known purpose.
fails: Pixels run from Custom HTML tags with copied code, so events, parameters or IDs drift and break without notice, or Custom HTML tags load scripts from vendors nobody can name.
validate: GTM read: tag types per platform; flag Custom HTML tags whose code loads fbevents.js, Snap tr, TikTok analytics or gtag, list what each sends, and list other Custom HTML tags with the domains they load.
action: Ask the developer to move each pasted pixel to the official template or the platform integration, and remove Custom HTML tags no one can explain.
done_when: No pixel runs from Custom HTML, and every Custom HTML tag left has a named purpose.
why_it_matters: Hand-pasted pixel code breaks quietly, so events and values can stop reaching the platforms and the signal campaigns learn from drifts from real.
selected_because: Backfill: tested in CRO audits (1 of 4 failed); template use is readable per tag.

title: Team and staff visits marked so they don't count as shoppers
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: The container sets traffic_type=internal (or a similar rule) for team and agency visits, or blocks primary tags for logged-in staff sessions, so GA4 can filter them.
fails: Nothing in the container marks team, agency or staff visits, so their browsing, test adds and test orders count as shoppers.
validate: GTM read: a traffic_type parameter on the Google tag, internal-traffic rules, and blocking triggers or exceptions for staff/admin sessions on primary tags. Whether staff are logged in on the live site is not visible; say so.
action: Ask the developer to mark team visits as internal and block primary tags for staff sessions, then turn on the internal-traffic filter in GA4.
done_when: The container marks internal visits or blocks staff sessions on primary tags.
why_it_matters: Team test orders and visits count as real buyers, so conversions can read higher than real, most of all on small stores.
selected_because: Backfill: current-tool check plus the staff-session exception, both readable in the container.

title: Page changes without a reload still send a page view
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: If the store moves between pages without full reloads (headless or app-like themes), a History Change or custom page-view trigger sends a page_view and pixel PageView for each new page; otherwise not applicable.
fails: On an app-like store only the first page sends a page view, so product views and later steps of paid visits go missing.
validate: Browser: check whether moving from home to collection to product reloads the document. If not, GTM read: History Change or custom page-view triggers on GA4 and pixel page-view tags.
action: Ask the developer to add a History Change or route-change trigger to the page-view tags.
done_when: Each page change on the app-like store sends one page_view and one pixel PageView.
why_it_matters: Missed page views after the landing page thin out the funnel and retargeting audiences, so the platforms learn from fewer product views.
selected_because: Backfill: high-impact where it applies; applicability and triggers are both checkable.

title: Live site runs the latest published container version
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: The gtm.js served on the live store reports the same version as the container's live version in GTM.
fails: A cache, CDN or hard-coded copy serves an older container, so tracking fixes you published never reach shoppers.
validate: GTM read: get_live_version (version id). Browser: the gtm.js request for the store's container ID on the visited pages and the version it reports; flag a mismatch.
action: Ask the developer to clear the cache or remove the hard-coded copy so the live site loads the published container.
done_when: The live gtm.js version equals the published version.
why_it_matters: If the live site runs an older version, fixes to Purchase or pixel tags don't take effect, so the platforms keep learning from the broken setup.
selected_because: Backfill: confirms that container fixes are live; version readable on both sides.

title: Snap, TikTok and Google event tags wait for their base tag
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: Where Snap, TikTok or Google event tags share a trigger with the base pixel or Google tag they depend on, tag sequencing or firing priority makes the base fire first.
fails: Event tags can fire before the base tag that loads the library, so those events are dropped at random.
validate: GTM read: tags sharing a trigger, their firing priority and setup/teardown sequencing; flag Snap, TikTok and Google event tags with no order set against their base tag. Meta order is checked with the Meta funnel tags.
action: Ask the developer to set the base tag as a setup tag, or give it a higher priority, for each event tag that needs it.
done_when: Every Snap, TikTok and Google event tag that shares a trigger with its base tag has an order set.
why_it_matters: Events dropped at random mean the platforms see fewer adds and purchases than happened, so reported ROAS reads lower than real.
selected_because: Backfill: a race condition readable from priority and sequencing settings.

title: Custom JavaScript variables behind value and IDs only return a value
group_en: Every sale counted once, with the right value
group_ar: كل Purchase يتسجّل مرة واحدة وبالقيمة الصح
pass: Custom JavaScript variables used for value, currency, items, order ID or event_id return a value and change nothing on the page.
fails: A Custom JavaScript variable pushes to the dataLayer, sets cookies or edits the page, so it runs every time a tag reads it and can repeat events or return an empty value.
validate: GTM read: the code of each Custom JavaScript variable referenced by ecommerce or conversion tags; flag dataLayer.push, cookie writes, DOM changes or network calls inside them.
action: Ask the developer to move any action out of these variables so they only return a value.
done_when: No Custom JavaScript variable used by a conversion tag does anything but return a value.
why_it_matters: A variable that acts each time it is read can repeat events or blank the value, so conversions and revenue the platforms see drift from real.
selected_because: Backfill: lowest-value pick; a quiet cause of wrong values, readable in the variable code.
